children: U.S. natural gas futures settle up 0.4% at $2.912/mmBtu, ending the week up 2.9% as warm summer weather extended well into September. Last week's 44 Bcf storage build was around half of the average for the week and "just really speaks to how strong power burn has been in September," says Andy Huenefeld of Pinebrook Energy Advisors. The strong power-sector demand and rising LNG feedgas flows are countered, however, by record U.S. production, with prices "really just bouncing back and forth in a relatively tight range,"he adds.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
